exposure: Sociodemographic factors (maternal race/ethnicity: Black, Native Hawaiian and Other Pacific Islander; maternal education; maternal age)
Participation in the Supplemental Nutrition for Women, Infants and Children (WIC) program
outcome: Late stillbirth (at 28 weeks or more of gestation)
cohort: The study included all singleton births in the US for 2014-2015, comprising 6,732,157 live births and 18,334 stillbirths.
finding: High maternal BMI and infants who were small for gestational age accounted for the largest proportion of late stillbirths, while participation in supplemental nutrition programs was associated with a significant reduction in stillbirth burden.
gest_age: 28 weeks or more of gestation (for late stillbirth outcome definition)
